input.rationale: With only 3 merit measurements, I tested the region near BiVO4 stoichiometry (Bi≈V), where the photoactive monoclinic BiVO4 phase at 2.4 eV is expected, and varied the Fe content. Index 30 (Bi 0.39, Fe 0.17, V 0.44; low Fe, slightly V-rich) gave 1.27e-6 A. That is about 2.4x index 22 and about 5x index 78, which is consistent with Fe hurting performance and a slight V excess helping.

Measured 2.6e-7 A: high Fe (0.35) strongly lowers photocurrent.

content.text:
I submitted **index 30** (Bi 0.39, Fe 0.17, V 0.44) as the best composition. It gave the highest photocurrent of the three I measured: **1.27 µA**. All 3 merit measurements are used. I didn't use any of the 5 XRD measurements.

| Index | Bi / Fe / V | Photocurrent |
|---|---|---|
| 30 | 0.39 / 0.17 / 0.44 | 1.27 µA |
| 22 | 0.43 / 0.16 / 0.41 | 0.53 µA |
| 78 | 0.30 / 0.35 / 0.35 | 0.26 µA |

- **Where I looked:** I targeted compositions with roughly equal Bi and V. That is where bismuth vanadate (BiVO4) forms, and it's the phase most likely to respond to 2.4 eV light.
- **Iron:** more iron clearly lowered the photocurrent. Index 78 has about twice the iron of the other two and gave the least current.
- **Bi vs. V:** with iron held low, the slightly vanadium-rich point (index 30) gave about 2.4 times the current of the slightly bismuth-rich one (index 22).

These trends rest on only three points and one measurement each, so treat them as suggestive. I can't tell how close index 30 is to the best composition in the library. For the last measurement I didn't take the Gaussian-process tool's suggestion (index 79). I picked index 30 because it had low iron and a little extra vanadium.
